candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record does describe neonatal lupus (maternal anti-SSa/Ro and anti-SSb/La antibodies, confirmed high-titer ANA in the infant, cardiac structural findings, pacemaker placement consistent with conduction disease). However, the reference diagnosis is 'lupus pneumonitis,' which specifically identifies the pulmonary manifestation driving the progressive bilateral ground-glass opacities, respiratory failure, and failed weaning despite negative cultures. C001 names the parent syndrome with a cardiac subtype (congenital heart block) rather than the pulmonary manifestation that is the requested final diagnostic object. It is compatible with the broader neonatal lupus family but misses the required pulmonary/pneumonitis specificity.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Neonatal lupus is the parent syndrome; congenital heart block is one manifestation, but the reference diagnosis specifically targets the pulmonary/pneumonitis component

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis 'lupus pneumonitis' in a neonate is an uncommon but documented manifestation of neonatal lupus; the case record supports this with progressive bilateral GGOs, respiratory failure, negative cultures, and failed weaning in the context of confirmed neonatal lupus serology.
Concurrent sepsis and cardiac disease (pacemaker) complicate attribution but the persistent pulmonary course with negative cultures and CT progression supports a non-infectious inflammatory etiology.
